Definition: properly, something dug, i.e. a (general) source (of water, even when naturally flowing; also of tears, blood (by euphemism, of the female pudenda); figuratively, of happiness, wisdom, progeny)
BiblicalUsage: mâqôwr is a fountain, a source of water and of life. In Jeremiah 2:13 God calls Himself the fountain of living waters, forsaken for broken cisterns, and in Jeremiah 17:13 those who forsake the fountain of living waters shall be ashamed. In Proverbs 5:18 a man's fountain is blessed, and in Zechariah 13:1 a fountain is opened to the house of David for sin and uncleanness. The word is the source itself, not the stream.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe mâqôwr names the God who is the source of all living water. I hold that every broken cistern I dig will run dry, and that the fountain opened for sin is the only water that cleanses.
